simple.meaning: צָלַע (tsâlaʻ) is a Hebrew action word meaning “to limp (as if one-sided).” BibleIQ anchors the English reading to this source verb before comparing its uses.
simple.biblicalBackground: This action appears 4 times in Genesis, Micah, Zephaniah, beginning at Genesis 32:32. The surrounding contexts include Israel.
simple.inThisVerse: In this verse, the tapped English word is source-aligned to צָלַע (H6760) in the Hebrew text.
simple.whyItMatters: Actions in Scripture show what people do, what God does, and how covenant faithfulness or rebellion is described. BibleIQ compares the action across its occurrences.
simple.summary: צָלַע (tsâlaʻ) / H6760 is traced through Genesis 32:32, Micah 4:6, Micah 4:7, Zephaniah 3:19 with source-language evidence and verse context.

definitions.full: H6760. tsala II. [ צָלַע ] verb limp (Arabic , Aramaic טלע Aph`el); — Qal Participle עַליְֿרֵכוֺ צֹלֵעַ Gen 32:32 (J; of Jacob); feminine הַצֹלֵעָה as substantive, of personified Judah as flock [ צאֹן ] Micah 4:6-7 , Zeph 3:19 .
definitions.rootNote: a primitive root; probably to curve; used only as denominative from 6763 ,

occurrences.englishText: Therefore the children of Israel don’t eat the sinew of the hip, which is on the hollow of the thigh, to this day, because he touched the hollow of Jacob’s thigh in the sinew of the hip.
and I will make that which was lame a remnant,

Behold,* “Behold”, from “הִנֵּה”, means look at, take notice, observe, see, or gaze at. It is often used as an interjection. at that time I will deal with all those who afflict you, and I will save those who are lame, and gather those who were driven away. I will give them praise and honor, whose shame has been in all the earth.
